story_text.value:
Solid 2.0 is now ready after five years, and a huge congratulations to Ryan Carniato and the entire Solid team.

I maintain Lily Design System which provides UI/UX components for Svelte, React, Vue, and more. I have just now completed Solid 2.0 components, and I'm seeking alpha testers to try the Solid 2.0 Lily tutorial and coach me on what needs fixing and improving.

https://lilydesignsystem.com/

This Solid 2.0 port is based on the React components with Claude Opus doing the translation, so I expect there will be AI errors along the way. Lily is free open source and I'm working on it for public sector social good purposes. I'm very keen on the new Solid improvements.

Any feedback, suggestions, constructive criticism, and the like, you can use the GitHub repo or email me directly joel@joelparkerhenderson.com.

story_text.value:
GTA 6 is here! I used to work in marketing automation, which mostly meant clicking around Klaviyo all day. So I built the obvious thing: an agent that does the clicking while I'm in Vice City.

It runs in my Chrome through an extension (using Playwright), using the tools I am already logged into. It can build a welcome flow in Klaviyo click by click, the way I would at work.

My favorite feature I added thus far? You can tell it to slow down and click more slowly :D Finishing a week of work by 10am is how you get caught.

The serious part is how good models have become at using a browser. A few months ago I posted my Google Ads MCP here (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49548962). I spent the summer building 65 tools for one platform. Now an agent just uses the same UI I use, on almost any site. Great use of my summer :D It's slower than an API, but it doesn't need anyone to build the API first (and slow is a feature, see above).

The plan has only one flaw: GTA 6 has no PC version, so the agent can't play it for me. Humans keep that one job.

I think this could be a real business, but I haven't figured out exactly how. I made pages for the obvious use cases and started running Google Ads to see what people care about (although I might stop them soon as the prices are crazy, 10 USD per click is nuts): https://shoppilot.ch/email-marketing/ https://shoppilot.ch/google-ads/ https://shoppilot.ch/seo/

Happy to hear your thoughts on this :DD If I reply slowly, I'm playing GTA. If I reply instantly, it's the agent.

story_text.value:
Frontier labs ship a lot. This gives me a handle on things. Also nice view of what the labs are prioritising (if release/research output is any indication)..

Made with GPT-6.2 Astra High. Initial prompt was a bit rambly, some refinement over time. It suggested 'scry' which I thought was a bad name so now its called Frontier Observatory, which is a tad less terrible.

Prompt:

You know what I'd like to build.. a visuliastion studio where I can monitor the pace of output across various groups/sub-groups etc from the two predominant frontier labs racing to AGI.. I think it would make for a fascinating experience. I want the aesthetics to be out-wordly artistic, we want this to be like a portal.. a crystal bowl of making sense of the past and predicting the future..

Also need a clever name. Single word. Minimal.

story_text.value:
Hey HN, I'm Salman, a research engineer at GDM Robotics on the team that built this robotics plugin.

Whether you're a robotics founder, data company, making RL environments, or just getting FOMO seeing all the cool robotics demos on X, you can just plug in a robot and start prompting away. The plugin we've written up includes skills that steer the model toward following best practices.

The benefits of using the plugin are: - fewer tokens (and therefore thinking time) needed to do bring-up the robot and to reach a successful attempt on your task - higher fidelity real-to-sim-to-real when creating MuJoCo assets and environments - leveraging strong motion planning, visual servoing, and collision avoidance

We have tested on SO-101, YAM, and Franka Duo, but you don't even need real arms to test it out. You can just create cool environments in sim and then prompt the model to control a simulated robot in the environment! (Just make sure to tell it not to use privileged sim state if you want to actually evaluate how good the perception and model intelligence is).

Just point your agent to the repo, good luck, and happy tinkering!

Let me know if you have any questions! Will answer anything here or feel free to post on the GitHub repo directly.

story_text.value:
I maintain a handful of archive libraries written in Rust and I had the crazy idea to throw them all together in a browser app, doing intense computational work, fully local in the browser. I've wanted to learn more about WebAssembly and this was a great opportunity to really see what it can do.

Nothing is uploaded, there's no server behind it. Everything processes local and it even works offline and on mobile. I made a 7z on my phone in airplane mode today.

There's a couple other tools like this out there, but they have sign-ups, ads, limitations. Archiver is a free tool for anyone and the only limits are what your disk can hold.

For 7z specifically, it also picks the best compression filters for every file in the archive based on the file type, which is really powerful when you're archiving large, mixed data (text+pictures+binary) folders.

Hope you enjoy.

story_text.value: Ruscal is a fairly-complete and well-tested Turbo Pascal to Rust transpiler, so you can run your old Turbo Pascal programs on modern computers. It supports mixing Rust and Turbo Pascal, embedding either way. It also supports graphics, including turtle graphics. I also included tools for pretty printing Turbo Pascal and converting old binary files to JSON. Great pain was taken to ensure accuracy with the original Turbo Pascal.

story_text.value:
This was made using a single prompt to Fable 5.2 on max thinking.

“Make a super creative 3D web game built in three.js based around a cute little ghost with a christmas hat on. No constraints, just the most fun playable three.js game you can think of, that has a playful on-theme user interface, will resonate with a wide audience (fantastic graphics, animation, polish, juice, interesting gameplay, novel ideas, etc)”

I’m pretty shocked at the quality. When I prompted Astra 6.2 the same way it gave me terrible output.

Now it could be that this sort of game is common and in the training data, but it’s pretty fun to play. It’s not perfect. 61,514,232 tokens across 123 model requests.

story_text.value:
Hey, I'm Matt. This is a free game I built in the spirit of the old internet. Just built for fun and no other reason. I built a version 2-3 years ago by hand. This time I built it assisted by Claude Code.

Every day you set a toggle. On/off, dials, etc. Every single one of them follows some piece of public data.

The board locks at 23:00 UTC and is scored. You then find out what was right or wrong. On some toggles there's also an indicator if you are hot or cold. The goal is to get them all right :).

Hints are given along at checkpoints along the way.

I have an open beta beginning November 30th. Would love to get feedback on the concept, what works, what doesn't, etc so that season 1 goes off without too many hitches.

title.value: Show HN: Toggles, a game based on analyzing data
